title: How it works: animated system diagram
summary: A concept or flow diagram builds itself: labelled nodes with simple icons appear one per beat at the tips of self-drawing arrows, packets travel along the arrows, the current node is lit and captioned, and the whole system lights up for a takeaway. The look of maths and engineering explainer channels.
techniques: self-drawing arrow paths with arc-length sampling
camera that frames the revealed nodes
row, column, snake and loop layouts
gallery_share: System and concept diagrams that assemble themselves are among the most common model-made explainer videos, from product onboarding to maths and engineering channels.
limits: Linear flows and single loops only: no branches, merges or labelled edges
2-6 nodes; six nodes in 9:16 use a two-column snake with smaller labels
Icons are a fixed set of 21 simple line drawings, not illustrations or logos
The template locks four nodes at 24 s so sound cues stay on the beats
Whether the diagram is correct is a human review; the renderer only checks timing, picture and loudness
